name: PPL Corp
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated electric and natural-gas franchises in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Rhode Island, with essential inelastic demand, FERC-regulated transmission, and a $23B capital plan guided to ~10.3% rate-base growth through 2029 — a durable, visible compounding machine. Capped at 6 because regulators (Pennsylvania PUC, Kentucky PSC, Rhode Island PUC, FERC) set the allowed return so there is no pricing power beyond rate cases, the plan is funded with debt (net debt $17,823M) plus about $3B of planned equity issuance that dilutes per-share compounding, Kentucky retains coal-fired generation with transition/recovery risk, and affordability politics rise as data-center load costs are recovered from existing customers.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: Durable PA/KY/RI regulated monopoly, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in 4 of the last 5 years and on TTM (capex exceeds OCF; normalized base -$0.90/share, TTM -$2.21/share) — Tier F on this screen; guided 6-8% EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
moat_for: Exclusive regulated electric and gas franchises in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Rhode Island — captive, essential-service customers
$23B regulated infrastructure plan 2026-2029 guided to ~10.3% average annual rate-base growth, with over 60% eligible for contemporaneous recovery
FERC-regulated transmission earns formula-rate returns; Pennsylvania/Kentucky large-load (data-center) demand adds a visible growth pipeline
Constructive recent regulatory outcomes — Pennsylvania settlement for a $275M annual revenue increase effective July 1, 2026 and a $233M Kentucky revenue increase
moat_against: Regulators cap returns — Pennsylvania PUC, Kentucky PSC, Rhode Island PUC and FERC set allowed ROE and recovery; no pricing power beyond rate cases
Growth is debt- plus equity-funded: net debt $17,823M and about $3B of equity needs projected for 2026-2029 dilute rate-base growth per share
Kentucky coal-fired generation carries retirement / environmental recovery risk
Affordability and large-load cost-allocation pushback as data-center spending is recovered in rates; refinancing the debt stack at higher rates
